topic: The Brachistochrone Problem: The Race of Curves

sections.title: Introduction: The Hook
lecture_lines: What is the fastest slide between two points?
Consider a straight line, a circle, and a curve.
Which shape wins the race under gravity?
[Asset: straight_line_vs_arc_vs_curve_race]
Gravity surprises us with the winning path.

Replace flat surface with a curve #FFFF00.
Highlight the time difference at target #FF0000.
Display the question: Which path is fastest? #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Prerequisites: Potential and Kinetic Energy
lecture_lines: Objects gain speed by dropping quickly.
Higher drops convert potential energy to velocity.
Faster early speed reduces total travel time.
animations: Show potential energy U = mgh formula #FFFFFF.
Animate energy conservation: U + K = constant #FFFF00.

sections.title: The Geometry of the Solution: The Cycloid
lecture_lines: The solution is a special geometric shape.
Meet the cycloid, traced by a rolling circle.
Imagine a point on a spinning bike wheel.
[Asset: cycloid_construction_animation]
The cycloid defines our winning curve.
animations: Draw a circle rolling to trace a path #FFFFFF.
Label the cycloid path as the solution #00FF00.
Compare the cycloid with straight path #FF0000.

sections.title: Mathematical Framework: Calculus of Variations
lecture_lines: Time depends on the path and velocity.
We minimize the integral of travel time.
Euler-Lagrange equations find the optimal curve.
animations: Define the functional integral I = integral(f) dx #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Conclusion: Real-world Synthesis
lecture_lines: The cycloid is the true Brachistochrone.
It also features the amazing tautochrone property.
All starting points arrive simultaneously.
[Asset: tautochrone_demonstration_animation]
Nature favors these elegant mathematical shapes.
